DEFINITION · qeva:1:coarse-graining@1

Coarse-graining

A many-to-one map from fine states to a smaller set of macro-descriptions, intentionally discarding distinctions.

editorialinformation · statistical-mechanics · learning · systems
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Coarse-graining keeps distinctions relevant at one scale or task and merges others.

EXACT

The compact statement

A coarse-graining can be represented by a non-injective map C:X→Y. States x1≠x2 with C(x1)=C(x2) are indistinguishable at the coarse level.

Example

Block averaging maps many high-resolution samples to fewer averages.

Boundary / caveat

Coarse-graining is not automatically intelligent or optimal. Whether discarded information is nuisance depends on an objective, observer, model, and scale.

Assumptions

  • Fine state space X, macrostate space Y, and map C:X→Y are specified.
